definitions.name: TGNNNodeMemSel
definitions.docstring:
V2 -- Local SELECTIVE memory admission + persistent node memory + global rehearsal.

This is the user's actual research idea, implemented as THREE separated stages instead
of the single soft gate of V1 (TGNN_Node_Mem):
  Stage 1  CANDIDATE SELECTION: events whose learned attention/importance a_i is in the
           top `sel_frac` of the batch, OR whose novelty >= `nov_tau`, enter the pool.
           Soft (sigmoid round the batch quantile) so the attention head earns a gradient;
           novel events are always admitted (set-union, not averaged).
  Stage 2  ADAPTIVE RETENTION FRACTION (phi): admit_i = sigma((S_i - theta)/T) restricted
           to candidates; a controller rate r_t in [R2_MIN, R2_MAX] sets the *target
           fraction of candidates* to keep (budget), decoupled from write strength.
  Stage 3  WRITE STRENGTH: EMA blend weight = admit_i * write_strength; the per-node memory
           transition is applied in CHRONOLOGICAL order (segment scan), so E1->E2->E3 chain
           (M1 from M0, M2 from M1, ...) instead of V1's "last-write-wins off the same M0".

Reads use batch-start memory (TGN convention, keeps GAT/CNN batched); only the lightweight
per-node EMA transition is chronological.  The controller (phi) is trained on a future-utility
signal via TBPTT over K batches (its writes feed later-batch reads inside one un-detached
window) plus budget + redundancy; everything else is theta.  use_memory=False yields the
param-identical, 2-GAT TGNN_Q_A_C baseline (same module set, memory path simply bypassed) so
the two TGNNs match parameter-for-parameter at inference and differ only in the mechanism.

definitions.name: controller_parameters

definitions.name: _chrono_write
definitions.docstring:
Persist a batch of gated writes in per-node CHRONOLOGICAL order (fixes V1's last-wins
collapse).  Each event writes BOTH its endpoints (src then dst); the per-node EMA
M <- (1-w)M + w.x is a first-order linear recurrence, so each node's own event run is
folded with a SEGMENTED associative scan (Hillis-Steele: ceil(log2 L) fully vectorised
passes) instead of a Python loop over scan positions.  Identical result to the sequential
fold, but no per-position full-slice index_copy -- that loop ran once per event touching
the busiest node and copied the whole [G,128] slice each step, the hub-heavy bottleneck.
Fully differentiable in (w: phi, x: theta); deterministic (unique sort keys; only
where/mul/add, no division).

scripts.docstring:
TGNN_Node_Mem: a learned adaptive memory-admission TGNN for streaming APT detection.

Three time scales, deliberately separated:
  * sliding window (seconds-minutes): the causal 5-slot ego graph -> local context c_t,
    produced by the SAME frozen encoder as TGNN_Q_A_C (GAT + time + history-GRU + attention
    + causal temporal CNN).  Reused verbatim so the comparison isolates node memory.
  * persistent per-entity node memory (long-term entity history): one 128-d state per graph
    node (process node = src, host node = dst).  Read before scoring; written AFTER scoring
    with a *learned, differentiable* gate -- the novelty here, replacing the fixed 0.5 EMA of
    the frozen M factor.
  * global replay (training knowledge): a bounded reservoir handled by the TRAINER, kept
    separate from node-memory admission (see modal_dedale_mem.ReplayBuffer).

Admission (spec faithful, v1 minimal core):
  Novelty_i   = 1 - cos(c_i, M_{v_i})                     (per entity, high when unseen)
  Importance  = sigma(w_a . c_i)                          (learned attention/importance proxy)
  Uncertainty = entropy(softmax(logits_i))                (optional, gamma)
  S_i         = alpha.Importance + beta.Novelty + gamma.Uncertainty
  r_t         = r_min + (r_max - r_min).sigmoid(f_phi(s_t))   (adaptive rate, ~0.25 at init)
  g_i         = r_t . sigmoid((S_i - theta) / T)          (soft differentiable write gate)
  M_v'        = (1 - g_i).M_v + g_i . MLP_write(c_i)       (per entity v in {src, dst})

Two parameter groups the trainer optimises separately:
  main_parameters()       (theta): encoder, memory read/write, fusion, head  <- L_task + lambda.L_replay
  controller_parameters() (phi):   f_phi, alpha/beta/gamma, theta_thr, T      <- L_future + budget + redundancy

Efficiency (v2): the per-entity memory is a dense table M[n_nodes,128] and every operation
is vectorised.  Reads/writes run in CHUNKS of `mem_chunk` events (TGN-style batch-granular
memory): all events in a chunk read the memory as of the chunk start and their writes are
fused last-wins, eliminating the per-event Python loop (~50x faster).  Causality is relaxed
from per-event to per-chunk; the gate still earns a task gradient because chunk-0 writes feed
chunk-1.. reads within the same (un-detached) training batch.  The encoder is also trimmed to
`gat_layers` GAT layers (default 2) for the new arch; the baselines keep their own depth.
Set adaptive=False for the fixed-rate ablation control (g_i := r_fixed, no controller).

definitions.name: TGNNNodeMemSel
definitions.docstring:
V2 -- Local SELECTIVE memory admission + persistent node memory + global rehearsal.

This is the user's actual research idea, implemented as THREE separated stages instead
of the single soft gate of V1 (TGNN_Node_Mem):
  Stage 1  CANDIDATE SELECTION: events whose learned attention/importance a_i is in the
           top `sel_frac` of the batch, OR whose novelty >= `nov_tau`, enter the pool.
           Soft (sigmoid round the batch quantile) so the attention head earns a gradient;
           novel events are always admitted (set-union, not averaged).
  Stage 2  ADAPTIVE RETENTION FRACTION (phi): admit_i = sigma((S_i - theta)/T) restricted
           to candidates; a controller rate r_t in [R2_MIN, R2_MAX] sets the *target
           fraction of candidates* to keep (budget), decoupled from write strength.
  Stage 3  WRITE STRENGTH: EMA blend weight = admit_i * write_strength; the per-node memory
           transition is applied in CHRONOLOGICAL order (segment scan), so E1->E2->E3 chain
           (M1 from M0, M2 from M1, ...) instead of V1's "last-write-wins off the same M0".

Reads use batch-start memory (TGN convention, keeps GAT/CNN batched); only the lightweight
per-node EMA transition is chronological.  The controller (phi) is trained on a future-utility
signal via TBPTT over K batches (its writes feed later-batch reads inside one un-detached
window) plus budget + redundancy; everything else is theta.  use_memory=False yields the
param-identical, 2-GAT TGNN_Q_A_C baseline (same module set, memory path simply bypassed) so
the two TGNNs match parameter-for-parameter at inference and differ only in the mechanism.

definitions.name: _chrono_write
definitions.docstring:
Persist a batch of gated writes in per-node CHRONOLOGICAL order (fixes V1's last-wins
collapse).  Each event writes BOTH its endpoints (src then dst); the per-node EMA
M <- (1-w)M + w.x is a first-order linear recurrence, so each node's own event run is
folded with a SEGMENTED associative scan (Hillis-Steele: ceil(log2 L) fully vectorised
passes) instead of a Python loop over scan positions.  Identical result to the sequential
fold, but no per-position full-slice index_copy -- that loop ran once per event touching
the busiest node and copied the whole [G,128] slice each step, the hub-heavy bottleneck.
Fully differentiable in (w: phi, x: theta); deterministic (unique sort keys; only
where/mul/add, no division).

scripts.docstring:
TGNN_Node_Mem: a learned adaptive memory-admission TGNN for streaming APT detection.

Three time scales, deliberately separated:
  * sliding window (seconds-minutes): the causal 5-slot ego graph -> local context c_t,
    produced by the SAME frozen encoder as TGNN_Q_A_C (GAT + time + history-GRU + attention
    + causal temporal CNN).  Reused verbatim so the comparison isolates node memory.
  * persistent per-entity node memory (long-term entity history): one 128-d state per graph
    node (process node = src, host node = dst).  Read before scoring; written AFTER scoring
    with a *learned, differentiable* gate -- the novelty here, replacing the fixed 0.5 EMA of
    the frozen M factor.
  * global replay (training knowledge): a bounded reservoir handled by the TRAINER, kept
    separate from node-memory admission (see modal_dedale_mem.ReplayBuffer).

Admission (spec faithful, v1 minimal core):
  Novelty_i   = 1 - cos(c_i, M_{v_i})                     (per entity, high when unseen)
  Importance  = sigma(w_a . c_i)                          (learned attention/importance proxy)
  Uncertainty = entropy(softmax(logits_i))                (optional, gamma)
  S_i         = alpha.Importance + beta.Novelty + gamma.Uncertainty
  r_t         = r_min + (r_max - r_min).sigmoid(f_phi(s_t))   (adaptive rate, ~0.25 at init)
  g_i         = r_t . sigmoid((S_i - theta) / T)          (soft differentiable write gate)
  M_v'        = (1 - g_i).M_v + g_i . MLP_write(c_i)       (per entity v in {src, dst})

Two parameter groups the trainer optimises separately:
  main_parameters()       (theta): encoder, memory read/write, fusion, head  <- L_task + lambda.L_replay
  controller_parameters() (phi):   f_phi, alpha/beta/gamma, theta_thr, T      <- L_future + budget + redundancy

Efficiency (v2): the per-entity memory is a dense table M[n_nodes,128] and every operation
is vectorised.  Reads/writes run in CHUNKS of `mem_chunk` events (TGN-style batch-granular
memory): all events in a chunk read the memory as of the chunk start and their writes are
fused last-wins, eliminating the per-event Python loop (~50x faster).  Causality is relaxed
from per-event to per-chunk; the gate still earns a task gradient because chunk-0 writes feed
chunk-1.. reads within the same (un-detached) training batch.  The encoder is also trimmed to
`gat_layers` GAT layers (default 2) for the new arch; the baselines keep their own depth.
Set adaptive=False for the fixed-rate ablation control (g_i := r_fixed, no controller).

V2 -- Local SELECTIVE memory admission + persistent node memory + global rehearsal.

This is the user's actual research idea, implemented as THREE separated stages instead
of the single soft gate of V1 (TGNN_Node_Mem):
  Stage 1  CANDIDATE SELECTION: events whose learned attention/importance a_i is in the
           top `sel_frac` of the batch, OR whose novelty >= `nov_tau`, enter the pool.

           novel events are always admitted (set-union, not averaged).

           fraction of candidates* to keep (budget), decoupled from write strength.

           transition is applied in CHRONOLOGICAL order (segment scan), so E1->E2->E3 chain
           (M1 from M0, M2 from M1, ...) instead of V1's "last-write-wins off the same M0".

per-node EMA transition is chronological.  The controller (phi) is trained on a future-utility
signal via TBPTT over K batches (its writes feed later-batch reads inside one un-detached

scripts.docstring:
TGNN_Node_Mem: a learned adaptive memory-admission TGNN for streaming APT detection.

Three time scales, deliberately separated:
  * sliding window (seconds-minutes): the causal 5-slot ego graph -> local context c_t,
    produced by the SAME frozen encoder as TGNN_Q_A_C (GAT + time + history-GRU + attention
    + causal temporal CNN).  Reused verbatim so the comparison isolates node memory.
  * persistent per-entity node memory (long-term entity history): one 128-d state per graph
    node (process node = src, host node = dst).  Read before scoring; written AFTER scoring
    with a *learned, differentiable* gate -- the novelty here, replacing the fixed 0.5 EMA of
    the frozen M factor.
  * global replay (training knowledge): a bounded reservoir handled by the TRAINER, kept
    separate from node-memory admission (see modal_dedale_mem.ReplayBuffer).

Admission (spec faithful, v1 minimal core):
  Novelty_i   = 1 - cos(c_i, M_{v_i})                     (per entity, high when unseen)
  Importance  = sigma(w_a . c_i)                          (learned attention/importance proxy)
  Uncertainty = entropy(softmax(logits_i))                (optional, gamma)
  S_i         = alpha.Importance + beta.Novelty + gamma.Uncertainty
  r_t         = r_min + (r_max - r_min).sigmoid(f_phi(s_t))   (adaptive rate, ~0.25 at init)
  g_i         = r_t . sigmoid((S_i - theta) / T)          (soft differentiable write gate)
  M_v'        = (1 - g_i).M_v + g_i . MLP_write(c_i)       (per entity v in {src, dst})

Two parameter groups the trainer optimises separately:
  main_parameters()       (theta): encoder, memory read/write, fusion, head  <- L_task + lambda.L_replay
  controller_parameters() (phi):   f_phi, alpha/beta/gamma, theta_thr, T      <- L_future + budget + redundancy

Efficiency (v2): the per-entity memory is a dense table M[n_nodes,128] and every operation
is vectorised.  Reads/writes run in CHUNKS of `mem_chunk` events (TGN-style batch-granular
memory): all events in a chunk read the memory as of the chunk start and their writes are
fused last-wins, eliminating the per-event Python loop (~50x faster).  Causality is relaxed
from per-event to per-chunk; the gate still earns a task gradient because chunk-0 writes feed
chunk-1.. reads within the same (un-detached) training batch.  The encoder is also trimmed to
`gat_layers` GAT layers (default 2) for the new arch; the baselines keep their own depth.
Set adaptive=False for the fixed-rate ablation control (g_i := r_fixed, no controller).

scripts.docstring:
Build a labeled, time-ordered DEDALE Windows-host dataset (winlogbeat/Sysmon) + causal
ego-graphs on the Modal Volume, for the GNN-vs-TGNN component study.

Design (all recorded in audit.json):
  * Modeling window = [min,max] @timestamp of the class-1 malicious client events, i.e. the
    active-attack period. Detecting the ~9.5k malicious events among same-host benign traffic.
  * Hosts = the victim clients (CLIENT1, CLIENT2) where both classes exist, so host identity
    is not discriminative (it is used only for graph connectivity, never as a feature).
  * Label = 1 iff the event matches a class-1 malicious record (external join; the label is
    NOT derived from any feature). MITRE/rule fields are absent from the raw logs.
  * Benign events in-window are reservoir-subsampled to neg_per_pos * positives; ALL positives
    are kept. Subsampling is identical for both models, so the paired comparison stays fair.
  * Chronological 60/20/20 split; every split is asserted to contain both classes.
Runs on Modal (the 27 GB winlogbeat zip lives on the Volume). No GPU, no training here.

  # Persistent deployment (recommended for long jobs):
  modal deploy dedale_data.py --name tg-detect-dedale-data

  # Launch the deployed Function asynchronously; this returns immediately.
  python dedale_data.py --spawn --neg-per-pos 15 --out-name dedale_host

  # Alternative interactive run (terminal lifetime matters unless detached):
  python -m modal run dedale_data.py --neg-per-pos 25

scripts.docstring:
TG-Detect vs Pomsathit (2025) — honest head-to-head on REAL data (CTU-13).

Protocols
─────────
P-temporal  : per scenario, strict chronological 60/15/25 train/val/test.
P-family    : leave-one-malware-family-out (train families != test family).

Models (all receive IDENTICAL 22-dim causal features and identical budgets)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  LogReg          tabular control — leakage gate
  HistGB          tabular control — strong non-graph baseline
  Pomsathit_GCN   3-layer GCN, hidden 128, attention aggregation, softmax
                  classification, 10% reservoir rehearsal buffer, operating on
                  time-window snapshot graphs (as in the paper).
  TGDetect_TGN    continuous-time: vectorised memory bank with risk-modulated
                  decay, multi-resolution time encoder, causal (dt>0) masked
                  temporal attention.

Eval hygiene
────────────
  * threshold chosen on VALIDATION only, never on test
  * AUC-PR is primary (prevalence is <1%); ROC-AUC, MCC, F1, P, R, FPR/day too
  * multiple seeds -> mean +- std; bootstrap CI on the TGN-minus-GCN delta
  * McNemar paired test on the test-set decisions
  * inference latency measured as ms/event with no_grad, separate from training

Run:
  modal run modal_bench_real.py::bench
  modal run modal_bench_real.py::bench --protocol family --seeds 3

definitions.name: feature_mask
definitions.docstring:
A (FEAT_IN,) float32 vector of 1.0 (keep) / 0.0 (drop).

Masking by MULTIPLYING AFTER STANDARDISATION, rather than by slicing the
tensor, is deliberate: FEAT_IN stays 22, every layer shape is unchanged, the
context cache stays valid, and all eight V2 superset proofs keep working. A
column that is identically zero after standardisation carries exactly zero
information, so this is a true ablation and not an approximation.

definitions.name: _ewma
definitions.docstring:
Bias-corrected EWMA along axis 0, vectorised as a first-order IIR filter.

y[n] = a*x[n] + (1-a)*y[n-1]. Done with lfilter so 6M events cost a C pass
rather than a Python loop. An EWMA is O(1) state per feature, so everything
here is implementable in a live streaming detector.

definitions.name: _group_cumcount

definitions.name: build_context
definitions.docstring:
Return (XZ, C), both strictly causal — every value at event i is derived
from events < i only. No leakage, and no peeking at the test marginal (unlike
a batch rank transform, which is why variant D is not deployable).

  XZ : (n, 22*len(scales)) causal EWMA z-score of every feature at every
       timescale. Stationary by construction: "unusual relative to now",
       not "large". Scales are concatenated in the order given.
  C  : (n, 13) the regime descriptor
         0  log1p(events seen so far)
         1  log1p(seconds elapsed)
         2  log1p(distinct nodes seen so far)
         3  log trailing event rate   (events/sec over the last `window`)
         4  trailing new-node rate    (fraction of events introducing a node)
         5..9  EWMA mean of each CUMULATIVE column at scale Z_REF = the
               current reference frame, i.e. what "high" means right now
        10  log1p(distinct sources that have contacted THIS dst so far)
              -> a C2 server accumulates many distinct callers; this is the
                 temporal build-up of the star that a snapshot GCN sees only
                 as a static shape
        11  log1p(prior contacts on THIS exact directed pair)
              -> beacon persistence
        12  trailing new-pair rate (network churn / scanning)

definitions.name: prior_adapt
definitions.docstring:
Saerens-Latinne-Decaestecker EM prior correction.

Attacks the 14x train->test prevalence jump at DECISION time. Uses only the
model's own predicted probabilities, never test labels — but it is
transductive (it reads the batch of test scores), so it must always be
reported as a separate column, never folded into the headline number.

NOTE the transform is strictly MONOTONE in p, so it cannot change AUC-PR or
ROC-AUC at all. It fixes thresholds, calibration, recall and F1. It cannot fix
an inverted ranking — that needs the architecture side (z-channel + FiLM).

!! TWO PRECONDITIONS, BOTH LEARNED THE HARD WAY !!

1. p MUST BE CALIBRATED. Fed overconfident scores whose mean sat far above
   pi_ref, the EM ran away to pi = 1.0, collapsing every score to exactly 1.0
   and DESTROYING the ranking. Our graph models train with POS_W = 20 and the
   tabular controls use class_weight="balanced"; both deliberately distort
   calibration, so isotonic/Platt recalibration on validation comes FIRST.

2. pi_ref MUST BE THE PREVALENCE OF THE SET THE CALIBRATOR WAS FIT ON — the
   validation prevalence — NOT the training prevalence. Isotonic fitted on val
   returns P(y=1|s) under the val prior, so that is the prior the EM must be
   told to correct away from. Measured on a fixture (true test pi = 0.0536):
       raw scores,        pi_ref = pi_train 0.0049 -> pi_hat 0.5000  BOUND HIT
       isotonic on val,   pi_ref = pi_train 0.0049 -> pi_hat 0.5000  BOUND HIT
       isotonic on val,   pi_ref = pi_val   0.0233 -> pi_hat 0.0860  ok
   SLD still overshoots (0.086 vs 0.054) when the classifier is imperfect;
   report pi_hat next to the true value rather than claiming it is exact.

Guarded accordingly: pi is clamped to (0, pi_max] each step, updates are
damped, and `hit_bound` is returned so a divergence can never be reported as
a result by accident.

Returns (p_adjusted, pi_estimated, hit_bound).

definitions.name: PomsathitGCN
definitions.docstring:
3-layer GCN, hidden 128, attention aggregation, softmax head, on window

definitions.name: TGDetectTGN
definitions.docstring:
Baseline aggregation PLUS multi-resolution time encoding and a per-node

definitions.name: TGDetectDrift
definitions.docstring:
TG-Detect + explicit drift semantics.

Three additions, and nothing removed:

  1. z-channel  - every feature is presented BOTH as its raw value and as
     a causal EWMA z-score against its own recent history. The raw value
     keeps the absolute information ("5,000 distinct destinations"); the
     z-score supplies the stationary view ("unusual for right now").

  2. FiLM conditioning - the regime vector c generates a per-dimension
     scale and shift applied to the feature embedding. This is the direct
     mechanism by which the network can learn that a feature MEANS
     something different early in a capture than it does late: high
     fanout is a busy server at t=0 and a scanning bot at t=T.

  3. c is also concatenated into the classification head, so the decision
     boundary itself is regime-aware.

The final FiLM layer is zero-initialised and applied as (1+gamma), so at
initialisation this model is EXACTLY TGDetectTGN. The superset property is
therefore provable, not asserted, and any measured difference is
attributable to the drift machinery alone.

FROZEN AT ONE Z-SCALE AND THE BASE CONTEXT. build_context now emits
len(Z_SCALES) z-blocks and 3 extra synchrony dims, but this model
deliberately slices back to what it was benchmarked with, so the 13-scenario
numbers already on record stay comparable. The wider inputs are consumed by
TGDetectV2, where they are individually ablatable.

definitions.name: BeaconEnc
definitions.docstring:
Scale-free periodicity encoder for one directed pair. (Novelty N1.)

Inputs are per-(src,dst) streaming state, all read BEFORE the current event
is folded in, so this is strictly causal:
    dtp : seconds since this pair's previous event
    mu  : EWMA mean inter-arrival for this pair
    sd  : EWMA sd of inter-arrival for this pair
    n   : events seen on this pair so far

r = dtp / mu is the PHASE RATIO. A beacon of period T has r ~ 1, or r ~ k
when k-1 intervals were missed or netflow-aggregated -- and crucially this
holds REGARDLESS OF T. The existing `log_dt_pair` feature cannot express
that: a 30 s beacon and a 3600 s beacon land in different places, so the
model has to learn each period separately and none of them transfer to a new
family. r transfers.

cos(2*pi*k*r) for k = 1..H is a comb (Dirichlet) filter: every harmonic
equals +1 at integer r and they cancel elsewhere. This is phase folding, the
standard periodicity test in signal processing, applied per pair instead of
per capture.

MEASURED channel separation d' (periodic vs Poisson at the same mean
interval, running the runner's exact EWMA recursion, so the mu/sd handed in
are noisy estimates rather than ground truth):

    channel   clean  jit10  jit25  jit37  jit50  miss20%+jit25
    cv         6.91   6.49   5.85   5.32   4.73      4.14
    cos1       1.93   1.79   1.04   0.40   0.03      0.32
    sin1       0.32   0.28   0.22   0.23   0.27      1.00
    comb       3.85   1.66   0.24   0.10   0.00      0.12
    log_mu     0.01   0.00   0.00   0.00   0.01      0.09

Three things that table settles:

  * cv (dispersion) is the workhorse and it survives 50% jitter, where all
    phase information is gone. Real C2 jitters heavily -- Cobalt Strike's
    sleep jitter is configurable to 0-99% -- so this is the channel that
    makes N1 viable rather than a clean-lab trick.
  * cos1 is the jitter-robust PHASE channel. The comb collapses past ~10%
    jitter because high harmonics sinc-null out at particular jitter widths
    (cos2 is 0.014 at 25% jitter while cos3 is 0.177). The comb is kept as
    an interpretable summary ONLY; the raw harmonics are what the network
    should use, and it gets them.
  * sin1 is the channel that lights up for MISSED intervals (0.32 -> 1.00),
    because dropped beacons inflate mu and shift the phase. Keeping both
    quadratures is therefore not decoration.
  * log_mu is flat at ~0.00, which PROVES the encoder is scale-free: it is
    not secretly re-detecting "short intervals", which log_dt_pair already
    gives the model.

definitions.name: TGDetectV2
definitions.docstring:
Composable upgrades over TGDetect_TGN, one flag per hypothesis.

    zs     : 0 | 1 | 3   width of the causal z-channel (N4)
    film   : bool        regime conditioning + regime-aware head (N4)
    sync   : bool        include the 3 synchrony/fan-in ctx dims (N5)
    pair   : bool        per-(src,dst) GRU memory (N2)
    beacon : bool        scale-free phase encoding (N1)

EVERY extra input enters through a ZERO-INITIALISED projection ADDED to the
base embedding, and no base parameter is renamed or resized. Two consequences
that matter more than they look:

  1. For ANY flag combination this model is EXACTLY TGDetect_TGN at
     initialisation. The superset claim is a one-line test
     (load the base state_dict with strict=False, compare logits) instead of
     the manual weight surgery TGDetect_Drift needs.

  2. Flags are therefore genuinely COMBINABLE. Turning two on cannot
     interact through a changed input layout, so a combined run measures
     the interaction of the mechanisms, not of the plumbing.

definitions.name: PlainMLP
definitions.docstring: No graph, no memory, no time. Isolates neural-vs-tree from graph value.

definitions.name: TGDetectRobust
definitions.docstring:
TG-Detect + two changes aimed at ONE measured failure: cross-family transfer.

THE OBSERVATION. On leave-one-family-out (hold out Neris) TGDetect_TGN scored
MACRO AUC-PR 0.5019 against Pomsathit_GCN's 0.6162 -- a 3.3-SE loss -- and the
whole gap came from ONE capture, s09 (Neris, 16.6% prevalence): 0.2554 vs
0.7799. s01 and s02 were a tie. Several per-capture ROCs came in BELOW 0.5
(TGN on s09: 0.4056; Drift on s01: 0.4850). Below 0.5 is not underfitting --
underfitting gives exactly 0.5. Below 0.5 means the model learned a real
relationship whose SIGN is inverted in the new family.

WHAT INVERTS. The GRU recurrence is m_t = (1-z)*m_{t-1} + z*tanh(.) with
m_0 = 0. A fresh host sits at the origin; a much-visited host has been dragged
toward an attractor. So ||m|| increases monotonically with the host's event
count: the memory NORM is an activity-volume proxy. That is the same
non-transferable quantity as log_src_prior_count -- except it is smuggled in
through MEM=128 continuous dimensions, where no feature mask can reach it.
Train prevalence 0.749% vs s09's 16.6% means every host in s09 is driven far
past any magnitude regime seen in training, so a decision rule keyed on
magnitude does not merely weaken, it flips. Pomsathit_GCN has no memory, hence
nothing to invert -- which is exactly why the simpler model won.

FIX 1, memnorm: read the memory's DIRECTION, not its magnitude.
    Write m = ||m|| * m_hat. The direction says WHAT KIND of behaviour the host
    has shown; the magnitude says HOW MUCH. Only the second is
    environment-specific, so drop it from the read path.
    LayerNorm does this exactly. For any a > 0 and any b,
        LN(a*m + b*1) = ((a*m + b*1) - (a*mu + b)*1) / (a*sigma) * g + beta
                      = (m - mu*1)/sigma * g + beta = LN(m).
    This is an algebraic identity, not an empirical hope: ANY per-host affine
    rescaling of memory intensity -- precisely what changes when the traffic
    level or the malicious fraction changes -- leaves the memory CONTENT
    untouched. The magnitude is not deleted from the system; TGDetectDrift
    already carries explicit maturity/rate terms in its context vector c, which
    is the right place for "how much", because c is regime-normalised.

    Applied as a GATED RESIDUAL with a zero-initialised gate:
        m_read = m + alpha * (LN(m) - m),   alpha init 0
    so at initialisation this model is BIT-IDENTICAL to TGDetect_TGN and the
    superset proof still holds. alpha is per-dimension, so the optimiser can
    keep magnitude in the dimensions where it is genuinely informative and
    discard it elsewhere -- it is not forced to choose globally.

FIX 2, memdrop: give the architecture a FLOOR.
    With probability p, zero the memory read for the whole batch (rescaling by
    1/(1-p) so the expectation is unchanged). Two consequences:

    (a) Regularisation, and a targeted one. Dropout on a pathway is equivalent
        in the linearised regime to an L2 penalty on that pathway's weights
        with coefficient proportional to p/(1-p) times the pathway's input
        second moment. The pathway here is EXACTLY the domain-fragile one, so
        the shrinkage lands on the weights whose inputs go out of distribution
        at test time, and on no others.

    (b) The structural point, which matters more. It forces the MEMORYLESS
        sub-model to be a competent classifier in its own right. TGDetect_TGN
        is a superset of Pomsathit_GCN in CAPACITY but had no guarantee of
        being one in PERFORMANCE: nothing in the ERM objective required the
        no-memory pathway to work, so under family shift the model could and
        did fall BELOW a strictly weaker architecture. With memdrop, the worst
        case is "memory is useless on this family", and the model degrades TO
        the time-blind baseline rather than through it.

    Dropped per batch, not per row, so every event in a batch sees a consistent

scripts.docstring:
Shared definitions for every TG-Detect Modal app.

Two reasons this file exists:

1. ONE image definition. The pip layer is content-addressed, so as long as this
   package list does not change, no app ever rebuilds it again. Every other
   module imports IMAGE from here instead of declaring its own.

2. The drift machinery. We do NOT drop features whose meaning changes over the
   stream — that throws away real signal (a host that has contacted 5,000
   distinct destinations IS suspicious). Instead we give the model the means to
   understand that the meaning is regime-dependent:

     * a causal EWMA z-score channel  -> "how unusual is this value RIGHT NOW"
     * a causal context vector        -> "what regime are we in"
     * FiLM conditioning              -> lets the network re-interpret every
                                         feature dimension as a function of the
                                         regime, which is literally the
                                         statement 'the meaning can change'
     * online prior adaptation        -> absorbs the prevalence shift at
                                         decision time instead of at feature time

The raw feature is always kept alongside its contextual view. Nothing is discarded.

Real-data acquisition + causal normalisation on Modal.

Source: CTU-13 (Stratosphere IPS / CVUT), 13 scenarios of labelled bidirectional
NetFlow. Chosen because it is the only APT/botnet corpus with (a) direct HTTP
download, (b) per-record ground-truth labels, (c) real wall-clock timestamps,
(d) multiple distinct malware families => genuine domain shift.

Guarantees enforced here (these are what the old synthetic pipeline violated):
  * Every feature is computed STRICTLY CAUSALLY: streaming state is read to
    build event i's vector, then updated with event i. No future information.
  * No feature encodes the label, the actor namespace, or any generator secret.
    All 22 features are derivable from a raw NetFlow record + past history.
  * Node identity is scoped per scenario ((scenario, ip) -> id), so no model can
    transfer "this IP is the bot" across scenarios.
  * Background traffic is KEPT. Prevalence is whatever the capture really is.

scripts.docstring:
Three-time-scale node-memory experiment on the DEDALE host 15:1 reservoir build.

Retests, head to head on ONE dataset (prepared/dedale_host_mem, which additionally stores the
per-event entity ids src/dst needed for node memory), three PARAMETER-MATCHED arms under one
threshold-honest protocol plus a latency matrix.  Both TGNNs use 2 GAT layers and the identical
module set, so they match parameter-for-parameter at inference and differ only in the mechanism
(training may differ -- the baseline is batched, the memory arm streams):

  GNN_H               GAT backbone + global rehearsal only            (window, no node memory)
  TGNN_Q_A_C          + time + history-GRU + attention + causal CNN   (the strong incumbent;
                      built from the memory arch with the memory path bypassed -> param-identical)
  TGNN_Node_Mem_Sel   same 2-GAT encoder + LOCAL SELECTIVE memory admission (the new idea):
                      Stage-1 top-rho attention UNION novel -> candidate pool; Stage-2 adaptive
                      retention fraction r_t in [0.10,0.30] (phi, future-utility + budget +
                      redundancy); Stage-3 chronological per-node EMA write of strength g.

Honest protocol (identical to the incumbent run): model selection on max validation PR-AP;
test PR-AP / ROC-AUC (threshold-free) + F1 at 0.5 / val-frozen / test-oracle thresholds + the
full F1 curve + raw probabilities. Memory arms are scored by streaming the chronological prefix
so node memory is causally warm; replay stays memory-free so out-of-order rehearsal cannot leak.

definitions.name: load_streams
definitions.docstring:
Load the 13 capped streams, with the causal context attached.

The context cache is keyed by (scenario, cap, CTX_TAG) and lives on the
Volume, so the O(n) EWMA pass over ~6M events is paid once ever rather than
once per container.

CTX_TAG encodes the z-scales and the emitted widths, so widening
build_context automatically invalidates every stale cache file instead of
silently loading a 22-wide XZ into a 66-wide model.

`halflife` is retained in the signature because it is a modal.parameter() on
both Lab classes, but the z-scales are now the module-level Z_SCALES tuple; a
single EWMA could not be both responsive and stable, which is what motivated
the multi-scale channel in the first place.

definitions.name: suite_eta
definitions.docstring:
Rough wall-clock estimate, in seconds, printed BEFORE anything runs.

Costs are per model-seed at 6 epochs on an L4 over the Neris holdout, scaled
linearly in epochs. Unknown model names fall back to the TGN cost, which is the
expensive end, so the estimate errs long rather than short.

Two multipliers on top of that, both from added no_grad passes rather than
added training:
  select        one VAL pass per epoch. Val is ~0.96M events against train's
                ~3.84M, and a forward-only pass costs roughly a third of a
                training step per event, so ~8%.
  probe_oracle  one TEST pass per epoch as well, ~1.15M events, so ~10% more.

definitions.name: make_folds
definitions.docstring:
Build (train, val, test) segment lists.

A segment is (stream, warm_start, eval_start, eval_end): the runner replays
[warm_start, eval_start) under no_grad so memory and last-seen clocks reach the
state a live detector would be in, without scoring those events.

protocol="temporal"  60/15/25 chronological split inside EACH capture.
    This is the ORIGINAL and it is the easy one. The same capture -- and
    therefore the same botnet host IP -- appears in train, val and test. Since
    the feature set contains log_src_prior_count / log_dst_prior_count /
    log_src_fanout, a model can memorise "the busiest host in this capture is
    the bot" during training and simply recognise it at test time. That is host
    fingerprinting, not threat detection, and it needs neither node memory nor
    Δt -- which is precisely why a plain 3-layer GCN matched a TGN on it
    (0.9828 vs 0.9341 AUC-PR).

protocol="capture"   whole captures held out. Test hosts are never seen in
    training, so the fingerprint shortcut is gone.

protocol="family"    whole MALWARE FAMILIES held out. The test botnet family
    was never trained on. This is the protocol the base paper's own claim
    requires: they claim robustness "against evolving APT campaigns", and an
    evolving campaign is by definition one you have not trained on.

For held-out captures the first 20% is replayed as warm-up (not scored), which
is what deploying a streaming detector on a new network actually looks like.

definitions.name: last_write
definitions.docstring:
Deduplicate `idx`, keeping the LAST occurrence of each index, and gather
`vals` at those positions. Returns (unique_idx, val0_last, val1_last, ...).

Why this exists: `Tensor.index_copy` with DUPLICATE indices does not specify
which write wins, and on CPU with 8 threads it genuinely races. Measured on
2048 rows of width 128:

    op                          distinct results over 12 identical runs
    index_add                    1   (safe)
    index_reduce(amax)           1   (safe; max is order-independent)
    index_copy, duplicate idx   12   (RACES)

The node-memory writeback is `mem.index_copy(0, sb, nm)` and a busy source
appears many times per batch, so the whole streaming runner was
non-deterministic: the SAME model at the SAME seed, evaluated twice, differed
by 2.0e-02 in predicted probability. That silently inflated every seed-to-seed
standard deviation ever reported by this project and would have made the V2_Off
control impossible to interpret.

Deduplicating first fixes both problems at once. It is deterministic, because
torch.unique returns sorted output and an integer amax is exact and
order-independent. And it makes the semantics match what the code always
claimed: the most recent event for that node wins, which is the correct
streaming state.

definitions.name: mem_leak_probe
definitions.docstring:
Is a node's EVENT COUNT linearly decodable from its final node memory?

This measures the quantity that PART XIII asserted and PART XIV built
`R_MemHard` on top of, and it distinguishes two hypotheses that the algebra
`LN(a*m + b*1) == LN(m)` conflates:

  H_scale     the count rides the memory's MAGNITUDE. Then LayerNorm removes it
              and r2_ln collapses to ~0. `memhard` works.
  H_rotate    the GRU's retention gates z_j differ across dimensions, so
              E[m_k] = (1 - z**k) * n_bar is a k-dependent DIAGONAL reweighting.
              The memory DIRECTION rotates with k. LayerNorm is invariant to
              rescaling, not to rotation, so r2_ln stays ~= r2_raw and `memhard`
              cannot work no matter how it is tuned.

Offline rigs (.labtest/research/e1_memory_leak.py on the analytic form, and
e1b_real_gru.py on a real torch.nn.GRUCell) came down hard on H_rotate: at
retention 0.847 LayerNorm removed 1.5% of the leak, at 0.974 it removed 2.1%.
Those are SYNTHETIC. This function is the same question asked of the trained
weights, and it is the measurement that decides whether R_MemHard / RD_MemHard
are worth any more GPU minutes.

r2_resid fits the rank-1 projection on one half of the nodes and evaluates it on
the other half, so it answers the DEPLOYABLE question -- "does removing a single
direction estimated from seen hosts also de-leak unseen hosts?" -- rather than
the tautology "does removing the direction that predicts t stop predicting t".

Crucially, k is the host's event count: OBSERVABLE at test time with no labels.
That is what separates this from the score-residualisation family, which needs
the SIGN of corr(activity, label) and therefore needs labels (see
.labtest/research/e7_identifiability.py, where that sign is proved
unidentifiable from unlabeled data).

Returns None rather than raising when there are too few eligible nodes, because
a warm-start segment can legitimately have almost no repeat sources and a probe
must never be able to fail a benchmark run.

definitions.name: gru_gate_stats
definitions.docstring:
Distribution of the GRU's RETENTION gate from the trained biases.

torch packs GRUCell gates as [reset, update, new] and computes
    h' = (1 - z) * n + z * h
so `z` (slice [MEM:2*MEM]) retains the OLD state and the memory horizon is
1/(1-z), NOT 1/z. Getting this backwards inverted the first reading of the
offline sweep entirely, so it is spelled out here.

Bias-only, i.e. the input-independent part of the gate. It is a proxy for the
operating regime, not the realised gate, and is reported as such: if z_mean is
small the memory is near-memoryless and the whole leak argument is moot.

definitions.docstring: Diagnostics and tabular controls. No GPU, so it is cheap to keep warm.

definitions.name: LabGPU
definitions.docstring:
Graph-model training. Same folds, same features, same budget for every
model, so any delta is attributable to the architecture alone.

definitions.name: info
definitions.docstring: Cheapest possible trigger: proves the container is warm and describes it.

definitions.name: diag
definitions.docstring: H1-H4 in one pass. Hypotheses are stated in RESEARCH_AND_FIXES.md PART VI.

definitions.name: _refit_scalers
definitions.docstring:
Recompute label stats and train-only standardisation for the CURRENT
folds. Split out of setup() so `bench(protocol=...)` can swap folds in a
warm container: leaving the old scalers in place would standardise the new
train set with the old one's mean, which is a silent leak.

definitions.name: _dro_state
definitions.docstring:
Fresh Group-DRO state: one weight per TRAINING CAPTURE, uniform at start.

Why captures and not families: DRO needs groups that are (a) numerous enough
that the max is informative and (b) actually different from one another. With
Neris held out there are 6 remaining families but 10 captures, and two of the
captures (the Rbot floods s10/s11) are wildly unlike the rest in prevalence --
which is precisely the heterogeneity we want the max to see. Grouping by family
would average those two together with the quiet Rbot captures and hide it.

Returns a plain dict, and it is rebuilt per model+seed inside _one so that
weights never leak across runs in a warm container -- the same class of bug as
the stale scalers that _refit_scalers was split out to prevent.

definitions.name: _vrex_state
definitions.docstring:
Fresh VREx state: one EMA of per-capture risk, plus the running mean of
those EMAs. See _run_epoch for the objective.

VREx (Krueger et al., ICML 2021) minimises  mean_e R_e + beta*Var_e(R_e).
DRO (already here) minimises max_e R_e; its guarantee holds only when the
test env is a CONVEX MIXTURE of training envs, which s09 (16.6% prevalence
vs 0.749% train mean) provably is not. VREx equalises risks, and equal
risks are stable under AFFINE-with-negative-coefficient combinations of
envs -- i.e. extrapolation, which is the regime s09 actually sits in.

Measured on the sign-flip toy (.labtest/research/e9_vrex_vs_dro.py, 15
seeds): when the shortcut's strength VARIES across training envs, test ROC
was ERM 0.396 / DRO 0.707 / VREx 0.775 -- VREx un-inverts hardest and
shrinks the shortcut weight most. When it does NOT vary, all three stay at
0.13: no objective can fix a consistently-signed shortcut, which is why
memhard (an architectural block) and VREx (an objective) are complements,
not alternatives.

definitions.name: _run_epoch
definitions.docstring:
One chronological pass. Every piece of state is READ BEFORE IT IS
WRITTEN for the current batch, which is what makes the whole thing causal.

`uses_ex` additionally maintains PER-PAIR streaming state:
    plast  last timestamp on this directed pair
    pmu    EWMA mean inter-arrival on this pair
    pm2    EWMA mean square, for the sd
    pn     events seen on this pair
    pmem   GRU pair memory (only touched when the model returns pm_new)
Cost is 5 extra hash-bucketed tensors; PAIR_BUCKETS*PMEM floats dominates
at 2^21 * 32 * 4B = 268 MiB, allocated once per segment like node memory.

`logit_adj` replaces POS_W reweighting with Menon et al. (2021) logit
adjustment: train on logit + tau*log(pi1/pi0), predict on the RAW logit.
The learned posterior is then balanced and INVARIANT TO THE TRAIN PRIOR,
which is the principled version of what POS_W=20 was hacking at -- and it
is the one intervention that can act on the *ranking*, unlike prior_adapt.

`dro` switches ERM for online GROUP DRO over captures (Sagawa et al. 2020),
with each capture as one group. See _dro_state for the argument.

definitions.name: smoke
definitions.docstring:
Cheap on-GPU sanity check. Verifies every model forwards with the shared
signature, and that TGDetect_Drift is EXACTLY TGDetect_TGN at init — the
superset property, measured rather than asserted.

definitions.name: bench
definitions.docstring: Train each named model on identical folds and report matched metrics.

definitions.name: suite
definitions.docstring:
Run a whole experiment plan back to back on ONE stream load.

Per-step `seeds: 0` means "use the caller's --seeds"; a non-zero value in the
plan overrides it, which is how the control step stays at 1 seed (it is an
identity check, so extra seeds buy nothing but GPU minutes).

Folds and scalers are rebuilt whenever protocol/holdout changes, and the
rebuild ALWAYS calls _refit_scalers: standardising a new train set with the
previous split's mean is a silent leak, and in a warm container that leak
would be invisible.

definitions.name: _suite_table
definitions.docstring:
One table across every step. This is the point of running a suite.

MACRO is the column to read (the pooled number is whatever the
highest-prevalence capture says), and the +-SE is what decides whether a gap
is a result: the loss this suite is trying to reverse was 3.3 SE, and an
earlier win of ours was only 1.9 SE and therefore merely directional.

definitions.name: _Reservoir
definitions.docstring:
Fixed-capacity uniform reservoir over training batches (Vitter's R).
This is the base paper's 10% rehearsal buffer, kept identical for every
model so continual-learning budget is never a confound.

definitions.name: _macro_ap
definitions.docstring:
Mean AUC-PR over the captures in `segs`, skipping degenerate ones.

Split out of _one because best-epoch selection and the oracle probe both
need it mid-training, and duplicating the offset walk is how the pooled and
macro numbers drift apart.

definitions.name: _val_select_score
definitions.docstring: The scalar that best-epoch selection maximises. Never touches test.

definitions.name: _one
definitions.docstring:
Train one model at one seed on the shared folds and score it.

Every knob that could become a confound is read off the class, never
guessed from the name: an earlier version inferred `is_tgn` from
name.startswith("TGDetect"), which would have silently disabled node
memory for every V2_* variant and made the whole ablation meaningless.

definitions.name: _ensemble_row
definitions.docstring:
A11: one extra row per model, from the seeds ALREADY trained. Free.

Ranks are averaged WITHIN each capture, not raw probabilities. Two reasons,
and both matter here:
  * AUC-PR and ROC are invariant to any strictly increasing transform of the
    score, so a seed's calibration is irrelevant information. Averaging raw
    probabilities lets the most over-confident seed dominate the mean for a
    reason the metric does not care about.
  * The seeds differ wildly in scale (F1-optimal thresholds ranged 0.10-0.62
    on the first suite), which is exactly the situation where rank averaging
    and probability averaging disagree.

Why it should work, and when it should not: write seed k's score as
s_k = f(x) + e_k with e_k the run-to-run noise that NOISE_MACRO measures. If
the e_k are even partially independent, the mean of K has noise variance
~sigma^2/K, so the signal-to-noise ratio rises by up to sqrt(K); for
equal-variance Gaussian class-conditionals AUC = Phi(d/sqrt(2)) with
d = Delta/sigma, and Phi is increasing, so the ensemble's AUC is >= the mean
seed's. The failure mode is honest and visible: if one seed INVERTED (ROC
below 0.5) its ranks fight the others, and the ensemble lands between them
instead of above them. Read the ensemble row against the seed spread, not
against the best seed.

definitions.name: _basin_report
definitions.docstring:
Report P(high basin) per model -- see PLAN.md PART 0.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Across all 15 recorded family-holdout runs the held-out
capture's AUC-PR is BIMODAL, not Gaussian:

    LOW  n=9  0.119 .. 0.372        HIGH n=6  0.511 .. 0.780

and a variance decomposition puts 87.3% of the spread BETWEEN the two modes
(0.05687) versus 12.7% within them (0.00830). corr(macro, held-out cap) =
+0.964, so the macro number is largely a readout of which mode the run landed
in. The two runs behind NOISE_MACRO = 0.22 are one per mode under a
byte-identical config -- that 0.22 is the BASIN GAP, not a sigma.

The consequence is the whole point: averaging more seeds does NOT shrink a
discrete mixture, it only estimates p = P(high basin) better. So the mean is
the wrong estimand and every MDE computed for it is answering the wrong
question. Fisher-exact power on p (0.17 -> 0.83) is 0.90 at n=12/arm, while
the mean at d=0.10, sd=0.199 needs n~300.

Reported for the WORST capture (min AP), which on family=Neris is the
held-out-family capture that actually discriminates -- s02 saturates at
0.98-1.00 for every model and carries no signal about the basin.

definitions.name: ablate
definitions.docstring:
Test N1..N5 individually AND combined against the same anchor.

Reported PAIRED: variant and anchor share every seed, so the per-seed
difference cancels the initialisation noise that swamped the 13-scenario
run (TGDetect_TGN's ROC-AUC had sd 0.2622 — larger than any effect we are
hunting). An unpaired comparison of two such means could not resolve a
0.02 AUC-PR effect at 3 seeds; the paired one can.

scripts.docstring:
TG-Detect LAB — a *deployed*, warm Modal app you trigger repeatedly.

Why this file exists
--------------------
`modal run` builds/attaches, uploads, runs, tears down. Iterating that way costs
minutes of container churn per experiment. This app is deployed ONCE:

    modal deploy modal_lab.py

and then every experiment is a cheap trigger from the laptop (see trigger.py),
with no image build, no re-upload, and no data reload:

  * the image comes from modal_common.IMAGE, which is FROZEN — the pip layer is
    content-addressed, so it is built once and never again
  * @modal.enter() loads the 13 CTU-13 npz files and the causal context ONCE per
    container, into instance state
  * scaledown_window keeps that container alive between triggers, so the 2nd..Nth
    experiment starts computing immediately
  * the expensive EWMA context pass is additionally cached to the Volume, so even
    a genuinely cold container skips recomputing it

Everything heavy runs here; the laptop only sends arguments and prints results.

definitions.name: AdmissionController
definitions.docstring:
phi: maps a per-event state s_t -> an adaptive write rate r_t in [r_min, r_max],
and combines (importance, novelty, uncertainty) into a candidate score S_t, finally
producing the soft gate g_t = r_t * sigmoid((S_t - theta)/T). All phi-only parameters.

definitions.name: TGNNNodeMem
definitions.docstring:
TGNN_Q_A_C-style encoder (GAT+T+Q+A+C, trimmed to `gat_layers`) + persistent per-entity
node memory with a learned, differentiable write gate.  adaptive=False -> fixed-rate control.
Fully vectorised: dense memory table + chunked batch-granular reads/writes (no Python loop).

definitions.name: TGNNNodeMemSel
definitions.docstring:
V2 -- Local SELECTIVE memory admission + persistent node memory + global rehearsal.

This is the user's actual research idea, implemented as THREE separated stages instead
of the single soft gate of V1 (TGNN_Node_Mem):
  Stage 1  CANDIDATE SELECTION: events whose learned attention/importance a_i is in the
           top `sel_frac` of the batch, OR whose novelty >= `nov_tau`, enter the pool.
           Soft (sigmoid round the batch quantile) so the attention head earns a gradient;
           novel events are always admitted (set-union, not averaged).
  Stage 2  ADAPTIVE RETENTION FRACTION (phi): admit_i = sigma((S_i - theta)/T) restricted
           to candidates; a controller rate r_t in [R2_MIN, R2_MAX] sets the *target
           fraction of candidates* to keep (budget), decoupled from write strength.
  Stage 3  WRITE STRENGTH: EMA blend weight = admit_i * write_strength; the per-node memory
           transition is applied in CHRONOLOGICAL order (segment scan), so E1->E2->E3 chain
           (M1 from M0, M2 from M1, ...) instead of V1's "last-write-wins off the same M0".

Reads use batch-start memory (TGN convention, keeps GAT/CNN batched); only the lightweight
per-node EMA transition is chronological.  The controller (phi) is trained on a future-utility
signal via TBPTT over K batches (its writes feed later-batch reads inside one un-detached
window) plus budget + redundancy; everything else is theta.  use_memory=False yields the
param-identical, 2-GAT TGNN_Q_A_C baseline (same module set, memory path simply bypassed) so
the two TGNNs match parameter-for-parameter at inference and differ only in the mechanism.

definitions.name: main_parameters
definitions.docstring: theta: encoder + memory read/write/fusion + head (trained on task + replay).

definitions.name: controller_parameters
definitions.docstring: phi: admission controller + importance feature (trained on future + budget + redundancy).

definitions.name: replay_logits
definitions.docstring:
Memory-free window classification for GLOBAL replay (anti-forgetting), kept strictly
separate from the per-entity node-memory stream so out-of-order replay never corrupts it.

definitions.name: _write
definitions.docstring:
Fuse this chunk's gated writes into the dense memory, last-write-wins per node.
Differentiable w.r.t. g (phi) and wc (theta); deterministic via a stable sort.

definitions.name: forward_events
definitions.docstring:
Score each event against its CURRENT per-entity memory, then stage a gated write.
Events are processed in chunks of `mem_chunk`: a chunk reads the memory as of its start
and fuses its writes last-wins (batch-granular causality).  Returns (logits[B,2], aux)
with per-event gate / novelty / rate for the controller's budget & redundancy losses.

definitions.name: main_parameters
definitions.docstring: theta: encoder + memory read/write + selection head + fusion + head.

definitions.name: controller_parameters
definitions.docstring: phi: retention controller only (future-utility + budget + redundancy).

definitions.name: _chrono_write
definitions.docstring:
Persist a batch of gated writes in per-node CHRONOLOGICAL order (fixes V1's last-wins
collapse).  Each event writes BOTH its endpoints (src then dst); the per-node EMA
M <- (1-w)M + w.x is a first-order linear recurrence, so each node's own event run is
folded with a SEGMENTED associative scan (Hillis-Steele: ceil(log2 L) fully vectorised
passes) instead of a Python loop over scan positions.  Identical result to the sequential
fold, but no per-position full-slice index_copy -- that loop ran once per event touching
the busiest node and copied the whole [G,128] slice each step, the hub-heavy bottleneck.
Fully differentiable in (w: phi, x: theta); deterministic (unique sort keys; only
where/mul/add, no division).

scripts.docstring:
TGNN_Node_Mem: a learned adaptive memory-admission TGNN for streaming APT detection.

Three time scales, deliberately separated:
  * sliding window (seconds-minutes): the causal 5-slot ego graph -> local context c_t,
    produced by the SAME frozen encoder as TGNN_Q_A_C (GAT + time + history-GRU + attention
    + causal temporal CNN).  Reused verbatim so the comparison isolates node memory.
  * persistent per-entity node memory (long-term entity history): one 128-d state per graph
    node (process node = src, host node = dst).  Read before scoring; written AFTER scoring
    with a *learned, differentiable* gate -- the novelty here, replacing the fixed 0.5 EMA of
    the frozen M factor.
  * global replay (training knowledge): a bounded reservoir handled by the TRAINER, kept
    separate from node-memory admission (see modal_dedale_mem.ReplayBuffer).

Admission (spec faithful, v1 minimal core):
  Novelty_i   = 1 - cos(c_i, M_{v_i})                     (per entity, high when unseen)
  Importance  = sigma(w_a . c_i)                          (learned attention/importance proxy)
  Uncertainty = entropy(softmax(logits_i))                (optional, gamma)
  S_i         = alpha.Importance + beta.Novelty + gamma.Uncertainty
  r_t         = r_min + (r_max - r_min).sigmoid(f_phi(s_t))   (adaptive rate, ~0.25 at init)
  g_i         = r_t . sigmoid((S_i - theta) / T)          (soft differentiable write gate)
  M_v'        = (1 - g_i).M_v + g_i . MLP_write(c_i)       (per entity v in {src, dst})

Two parameter groups the trainer optimises separately:
  main_parameters()       (theta): encoder, memory read/write, fusion, head  <- L_task + lambda.L_replay
  controller_parameters() (phi):   f_phi, alpha/beta/gamma, theta_thr, T      <- L_future + budget + redundancy

scripts.docstring:
Thin local client for the deployed TG-Detect lab.

Deploy once (only needed again when modal_lab.py / modal_common.py change):

    modal deploy modal_lab.py

Then every experiment is a trigger with no image build and no data reload:

    python trigger.py info
    python trigger.py smoke
    python trigger.py diag
    python trigger.py bench --models TGDetect_TGN,TGDetect_Drift --seeds 3 --epochs 6
    python trigger.py ablate --seeds 3 --epochs 4
    python trigger.py ablate --variants V2_All --seeds 5 --epochs 6 --logit-adj

The first trigger after a deploy pays a cold start (container boot + npz load +
causal-context build, and the context is then cached on the Volume). Subsequent
triggers land on the warm container and start computing immediately, which is the
whole point of deploy-and-trigger over `modal run`.

Results are printed here and also written to results/<cmd>-<timestamp>.json.

Long runs (`suite`, multi-seed `bench`/`ablate`) should be launched detached:

    python trigger.py suite --plan robust --detach
    python trigger.py poll <call-id>          # reattach any time, from anywhere

`.remote()` is client-attached: Modal cancels the input as soon as this local
process goes away (terminal closed, laptop asleep, network drop), which is why a
two-hour suite dies mid-step. `--detach` uses `.spawn()`, so the work is owned by
the server and survives the client.
path_references: SCOPE at which --decorr centres its correlation. 'batch' is the original and is left byte-identical. 'capture' centres on the RUNNING CAPTURE mean instead. Why it matters: by the law of total covariance, Cov(s,a) = E_b[Cov(s,a|b)] + Cov_b(E[s|b],E[a|b]), and a per-batch penalty sees only the first term. The activity columns are CUMULATIVE counters, so they ramp with time and batches are contiguous windows -- a time-ordered offline rig measured the split at 59.1%% within vs 40.9%% BETWEEN, i.e. batch scope is structurally blind to two fifths of the association it is meant to remove. See .labtest/research/e8_decorr_scope.py.

measure whether a host's EVENT COUNT is linearly decodable from its node memory: R2(log k) from the raw memory, from the LayerNormed memory, and after removing one rank-1 direction fitted on held-out nodes. This ARBITRATES memhard. LN(a*m+b)==LN(m) is a theorem, but it is invariance to RESCALING; if the GRU's retention gates differ across dimensions then saturation (1-z**k) rotates the memory DIRECTION with k, and LayerNorm is blind to rotations. Also prints the trained retention gate and the ||m||-vs-k curve: a FLAT curve with horizon ~1 means the memory has no horizon and there is no leak to remove, which is a different and worse finding. Costs one extra ridge fit per test capture, no extra training. See .labtest/research/e1b_real_gru.py and e9_probe_selftest.py.

V-REx objective weight beta (Krueger 2021): add beta*Var_capture(risk) so the model EQUALISES per-capture risk instead of just minimising the average. Complements --dro rather than duplicating it: DRO minimises the WORST capture's risk and its bound holds only inside the convex hull of training captures; s09 is a 22x prevalence EXTRAPOLATION outside that hull, where equal-risk (VREx) is the property preserved under affine env shifts. Measured on the sign-flip toy (15 seeds, VARIED shortcut): test ROC ERM 0.396 / DRO 0.707 / VREx 0.775. When shortcut strength is constant across captures the variance signal vanishes and VREx needs --memhard to lean on. Try 1.0. See .labtest/research/e9_vrex_vs_dro.py.

definitions.name: TGNNNodeMemSel
definitions.docstring:
V2 -- Local SELECTIVE memory admission + persistent node memory + global rehearsal.

This is the user's actual research idea, implemented as THREE separated stages instead
of the single soft gate of V1 (TGNN_Node_Mem):
  Stage 1  CANDIDATE SELECTION: events whose learned attention/importance a_i is in the
           top `sel_frac` of the batch, OR whose novelty >= `nov_tau`, enter the pool.
           Soft (sigmoid round the batch quantile) so the attention head earns a gradient;
           novel events are always admitted (set-union, not averaged).
  Stage 2  ADAPTIVE RETENTION FRACTION (phi): admit_i = sigma((S_i - theta)/T) restricted
           to candidates; a controller rate r_t in [R2_MIN, R2_MAX] sets the *target
           fraction of candidates* to keep (budget), decoupled from write strength.
  Stage 3  WRITE STRENGTH: EMA blend weight = admit_i * write_strength; the per-node memory
           transition is applied in CHRONOLOGICAL order (segment scan), so E1->E2->E3 chain
           (M1 from M0, M2 from M1, ...) instead of V1's "last-write-wins off the same M0".

Reads use batch-start memory (TGN convention, keeps GAT/CNN batched); only the lightweight
per-node EMA transition is chronological.  The controller (phi) is trained on a future-utility
signal via TBPTT over K batches (its writes feed later-batch reads inside one un-detached
window) plus budget + redundancy; everything else is theta.  use_memory=False yields the
param-identical, 2-GAT TGNN_Q_A_C baseline (same module set, memory path simply bypassed) so
the two TGNNs match parameter-for-parameter at inference and differ only in the mechanism.

definitions.name: _chrono_write
definitions.docstring:
Persist a batch of gated writes in per-node CHRONOLOGICAL order (fixes V1's last-wins
collapse).  Each event writes BOTH its endpoints (src then dst); the per-node EMA
M <- (1-w)M + w.x is a first-order linear recurrence, so each node's own event run is
folded with a SEGMENTED associative scan (Hillis-Steele: ceil(log2 L) fully vectorised
passes) instead of a Python loop over scan positions.  Identical result to the sequential
fold, but no per-position full-slice index_copy -- that loop ran once per event touching

definitions.name: TGNNNodeMemSel
definitions.docstring:
V2 -- Local SELECTIVE memory admission + persistent node memory + global rehearsal.

This is the user's actual research idea, implemented as THREE separated stages instead
of the single soft gate of V1 (TGNN_Node_Mem):
  Stage 1  CANDIDATE SELECTION: events whose learned attention/importance a_i is in the
           top `sel_frac` of the batch, OR whose novelty >= `nov_tau`, enter the pool.
           Soft (sigmoid round the batch quantile) so the attention head earns a gradient;
           novel events are always admitted (set-union, not averaged).
  Stage 2  ADAPTIVE RETENTION FRACTION (phi): admit_i = sigma((S_i - theta)/T) restricted
           to candidates; a controller rate r_t in [R2_MIN, R2_MAX] sets the *target
           fraction of candidates* to keep (budget), decoupled from write strength.
  Stage 3  WRITE STRENGTH: EMA blend weight = admit_i * write_strength; the per-node memory
           transition is applied in CHRONOLOGICAL order (segment scan), so E1->E2->E3 chain
           (M1 from M0, M2 from M1, ...) instead of V1's "last-write-wins off the same M0".

Reads use batch-start memory (TGN convention, keeps GAT/CNN batched); only the lightweight
per-node EMA transition is chronological.  The controller (phi) is trained on a future-utility
signal via TBPTT over K batches (its writes feed later-batch reads inside one un-detached
window) plus budget + redundancy; everything else is theta.  use_memory=False yields the
param-identical, 2-GAT TGNN_Q_A_C baseline (same module set, memory path simply bypassed) so
the two TGNNs match parameter-for-parameter at inference and differ only in the mechanism.

definitions.name: _chrono_write
definitions.docstring:
Persist a batch of gated writes in per-node CHRONOLOGICAL order (fixes V1's last-wins
collapse).  Each event writes BOTH its endpoints (src then dst); the per-node EMA
M <- (1-w)M + w.x is a first-order linear recurrence, so each node's own event run is
folded with a SEGMENTED associative scan (Hillis-Steele: ceil(log2 L) fully vectorised
passes) instead of a Python loop over scan positions.  Identical result to the sequential
fold, but no per-position full-slice index_copy -- that loop ran once per event touching
the busiest node and copied the whole [G,128] slice each step, the hub-heavy bottleneck.
Fully differentiable in (w: phi, x: theta); deterministic (unique sort keys; only
where/mul/add, no division).
